lines.text: Your headphones fight noise, with more noise.
Sound is just air being pushed and pulled. A wave.
A tiny mic on the outside hears it coming.
A chip flips it upside down. Every push becomes a pull.
Then the speaker plays that flipped wave, at the exact same moment.
Push meets pull, and they cancel out.
But it has to be perfectly timed. Arrive late, and the waves stack up instead.
That's why it kills a steady engine hum, but barely touches voices.
So the next time the world goes quiet, that's noise, fighting noise.
